- When sentiment is consistently negative (e.g., 0.00 or low values), model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecasts by 10–20% in such periods.
- After a sharp spike in sentiment (e.g., 1.00 or above), model often overshoots; cap forecast peaks at 1.5x the prior 7-day average.
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.33–0.67), model frequently underestimates; adjust upward by 5–15% if recent history shows upward momentum.
- Model exhibits strong lag in reacting to sentiment shifts — if sentiment turns positive after 3–5 days, forecast should be adjusted upward by 1–2 days.
- Mean reversion is strong in low-sentiment periods — if forecast is >2.5x historical mean, reduce by 20–30% unless sentiment is strong.
- In high-sentiment periods (e.g., 0.67+), model often overpredicts; apply downward bias of 5–10% if sentiment is sustained above 0.67 for 3+ days.
- Avoid forecasting spikes in sentiment >1.00 without confirming recent price momentum — if sentiment spikes but price hasn’t moved, reduce forecast by 20–40%.
